title: Salem Sends 97.28% of Its Class XII Students Into Higher Education
excerpt: A Collectorate control room, four rounds of career counselling and five admission camps lifted Salem from 91% in September to near-universal enrolment.
body:
• In Salem district, 34,374 of the 35,334 students who passed Class XII in 2025-26 have enrolled in higher education — 97.28%, up from 91% reported in September.
  • A district control room at the Collectorate tracked students who had not secured a place and intervened directly.
  • Five Uyarvukku Padi camps across Salem, Attur, Konganapuram and Mecheri produced 1,149 direct college admissions.
  • What this means for families: fewer than 1,000 Salem students are still without a placement, and the district's model — find every unenrolled student by name and counsel them — is the template Tamil Nadu is running statewide for all 5.44 lakh Class 12 students.

Nearly every student who finished school in Salem this year is going on to study further. Of 35,334 students who passed Class XII in 2025-26, 34,374 have enrolled in colleges or vocational training institutions — 97.28 per cent, the district administration has reported, according to The Hindu. The figure is up from 91 per cent in mid-September, when 32,166 students had secured places.

How Salem closed the gap

The last six percentage points were the hard part, and the district treated them as a list of names, not a statistic. District Collector K. Elambahavath set up a dedicated educational control room at the Collectorate to monitor enrolment and help students directly. The School Education Department identified 2,330 students who had not yet secured a placement and invited them to the Collectorate for the Perithinum Perithu Kel career guidance programme, run in four phases in late May, covering family counselling, certificate verification and help with engineering counselling and choice filling, according to Mirror Now. Five Uyarvukku Padi camps held across Salem, Attur, Konganapuram and Mecheri then produced 1,149 direct admissions for students who needed on-the-spot help applying.

https://x.com/the_hindu/status/2114385569711309163

Part of a statewide drive

Salem is the sharp end of a Tamil Nadu programme that aims to enrol every Class 12 student in higher education or technical training. The state directed all district collectors to run control rooms headed by officers of Deputy Collector rank, using education data to find students who had not applied, had failed or missed examinations, or had not registered for supplementary exams, and to intervene on the obstacles — certificates, scholarships, finance — that stop enrolment. Statewide, the drive covers 5.44 lakh students from the 2025-26 Class 12 cohort, including 3.55 lakh from government schools.

What happens next

Fewer than 1,000 Salem students remain unenrolled, and the district's own September experience — when 3,168 were still without a place — shows the remaining cases are the hardest: family finances, migration for work and failed examinations. The state drive runs through October, and Salem's 97.28 per cent sets the benchmark other districts will be measured against when final numbers are compiled.
